newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 9.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Tuesday:
- John Hume, leader of the Catholic Social, Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP), was seeking an immediate meeting with British Prime Minister Tony Blair to discuss the crisis in Northern Ireland.
- IDA Ireland representatives met senior Asahi management in Dublin yesterday to urge renewed talks over the future of a plant in Co. Mayo.
- The Competition Authority called on the government not to renew the Groceries Order, which bans all below-cost selling by food retailers.
- Ireland's Central Bank was expected to sit tight on interest rates despite the punt's fall against sterling.
- Dramatic new evidence affecting former Prime Minister Charles Haughey may be revealed to the Dunnes Payments Tribunal on Wednesday.
- The Irish National Liberation Army threatened to kill Protestants if an Orange Order parade down the Catholic Lower Ormeau Road in Belfast goes ahead on Saturday.
- Irish inflation figures due on Thursday could lead to a rise in interest rates.
